title: Rupee Closes at Six-Month High as Foreign Investors Return to Indian Equities
excerpt: The rupee closed at 93.9050 per dollar, its strongest since April, after nearly $3 billion of foreign equity buying in a week — including $1.6 billion on Thursday alone.
body:
• The Indian rupee closed at 93.9050 per US dollar on Friday, November 6 — its strongest level since April 22, according to Reuters, after touching 94.08 intraday, a nearly six-month high.
  • Foreign investors bought nearly $3 billion of Indian equities during the week, including about $1.6 billion on Thursday, after two consecutive months of selling.
  • The rupee gained 1.1% over the week, its best weekly performance in three weeks; it remains down about 4.5% in 2026 after a record low of 96.96 in May.
  • For remitters: the move from 96.96 to about 93.9 means each dollar now converts to roughly 3 rupees less than at the May low.

The Indian rupee closed at 93.9050 per US dollar on Friday, its strongest level since April 22, according to Reuters figures reported by BoldVoices. Intraday, the currency touched 94.08, a nearly six-month high, CNBC-TV18 reported. The weekly gain of 1.1% was the rupee's best in three weeks and made it the second-strongest Asian currency over the week.

What drove the recovery

Three forces lined up. Foreign portfolio investors returned: Reuters reported nearly $3 billion of foreign equity purchases during the week, including about $1.6 billion on Thursday alone — which CNBC-TV18, citing provisional exchange data via Reuters, called the biggest single-day purchase in nearly six years, following two consecutive months of selling. Crude oil prices fell sharply over the week, easing the pressure India's import bill puts on the currency. And the US dollar softened after the midterm elections, as market participants weighed whether a changed balance of power in Congress could constrain further US fiscal expansion. FXStreet's market report tied the inflow acceleration to a global sector rotation as investors questioned AI spending — money rotating out of AI-heavy markets and into Indian equities, alongside strong second-quarter corporate earnings in India.

"Much of the capital that left chased the US-led AI and semiconductor trade; some returns only if that trade cools."

— Akash Garg, Choice Wealth, as reported by The New Indian Express

Stabilisation, not yet a trend

The same FXStreet report carries the caution from Choice Wealth's Akash Garg: for flows to turn durable, the rupee must stabilise, crude must stay soft, clarity must emerge on a US-India trade deal, and Indian corporate earnings must deliver upgrades — for now, this is welcome stabilisation, not yet a trend. The year's ledger supports the caution. Even after this week, the rupee remains down about 4.5% in 2026, having touched a record low of 96.96 in May. A few sessions of inflows do not yet establish that the broader outflow pattern has permanently reversed.

What to watch next

Whether foreign buying continues is the central question, alongside crude prices, the dollar's direction after the midterms, and US jobs data due shortly. For diaspora households, the practical effect is immediate and mechanical: money sent home this week converts at around 93.9 rupees per dollar rather than the 96.96 available at May's low — a difference of about 3% on a large transfer, in the opposite direction from what remitters enjoyed earlier this year.
